claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends the repository-structuring strategies described in this guide (one package per repository, cohesive components) for publishing packages.
Following the recommended repository practices improves the reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed of packages an organization builds and consumes.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
The `pulumi package publish` CLI command exists and is documented at /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/.

Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.

A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type; a repository with multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights how Pulumi consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single Pulumi package are supported and expected, and ship together at the package's version.

The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry (at pulumi.com/registry/packages/eks/) bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with the supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
A single `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
The example repository layout places `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repo root and components under a `components/` directory.
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
It is technically possible to use a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way regardless of whether each component changed, which violates semver.
In a package with two unrelated components, an enhancement to ComponentA leads to release v1.1.0 and a breaking change to ComponentB leads to release v2.0.0, illustrating semver decoupling.

The Pulumi IDP Private Registry documentation exists at /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/ and the packaging-components guide has anchors #source-based-plugin-packages and #executable-based-plugin-packages.
A Publishing packages guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/ covering publishing mechanics.
